item.title: Deputy national security advisor is Canada’s new fentanyl czar
item.description: Prime Minister Justin Trudeau is appointing his deputy national security advisor to become Canada’s first fentanyl czar.

item.title: The Daily Brief | Trudeau gov gave Liberal-led international org millions
item.description: A Canadian international aid group bankrolled by nearly $180 million from Global Affairs Canada since 2015 counts four Liberal party donors in its leadership—including a CEO who once ran for a Liberal nomination under Prime Minister Justin Trudeau. Tune into The Daily Brief.

item.title: Exclusive: UWaterloo hiring only “woman-identifying,” gender minority STEM research chairs
item.description: The University of Waterloo is currently limiting the hiring of several science, technology, engineering and mathematics research chairs to only candidates who “self-identify” as women or another gender minority.

item.title: The Candice Malcolm Show | What are Mark Carney’s “Values”?
item.description: True North senior researcher Cosmin Dzsurdzsa joins the show to discuss his investigative series, ‘Carney’s “Values,”’ which focuses on the ideas presented in Carney's 2021 book “Value(s)” and how they reveal his vision for Canada’s future.

item.title: Carney, as head of the Liberal Party, would narrow gap between Conservatives and Liberals: poll
item.description: A new Leger poll indicates that the gap between the Conservatives and Liberals would disappear if Mark Carney were to square off against Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre in a general election.

item.title: Ford’s PCs pledge $50 million to strengthen Ontario’s border protection
item.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford says his government will contribute $50 million for patrol helicopters to beef up the province’s capacity to defend the border amid a tariff dispute with the United States.

item.title: Trump threatens up to 100% tariffs on Canada’s auto sector
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump is threatening as much as a 100-per-cent tariff on Canada’s auto sector, in addition to the threatened 25-per-cent tariffs now on hold.

item.title: Premiers travel to Washington in “charm offensive” to negotiate removal of U.S. tariffs
item.description: Canada’s premiers travelled to Washington, D.C. to negotiate with Republican senators, lawmakers and business groups in the hopes of persuading U.S. President Donald Trump to rescind his pledge to impose crippling tariffs on Canadian imports.

item.title: Former prime ministers call on Canadians to fly the flag like “never before” amid tariff turbulence
item.description: Canada’s former prime ministers have come together to call for Canadians to show their national pride Saturday for the country’s “flag day,” which will also mark the 60th anniversary of the maple leaf’s debut.
